resources.string: Ovulation is estimated this many days before the next period start. This is a calendar estimate, not a measurement or a reliable method of contraception.
Cramps may be strongest near the start, sometimes spreading to the back. Flow and tiredness can vary from one day to the next.
Bleeding may continue while cramps begin to ease. This is not a deadline: symptoms do not follow the same timetable for everyone.
Flow may become lighter near your usual end. Persistent pain, unusually heavy bleeding or bleeding longer than usual deserves medical advice.
Pain or poor sleep may leave you more sensitive or less patient. You may also feel your usual self. Tell others whether you want quiet, help or company.
Premenstrual irritability may start to lift, but stress and sleep also affect mood. Notice your own pattern rather than expecting a particular emotion.
Energy or interest in company may return, or you may still need rest. Neither response says anything about your personality or how you should behave.
Comfortably warm, wrapped heat and gentle movement may help. Stop any activity that worsens pain. Severe or worsening pain needs assessment.
Keep regular meals, fluids and sleep. Choose activity by comfort. Do not start supplements just because of a cycle day; ask about persistent fatigue or heavy bleeding.
Return to your usual activity at your own pace. Record the actual end of bleeding and what helped, so the next cycle can be compared with your experience.
